questions.question: Explain the terms personal assets, personal liabilities and net worth.
questions.expected_answer: Personal assets: things of value a person owns, e.g. house, car, furniture, savings, cash. Personal liabilities: amounts a person owes, e.g. bond, car loan, credit card, store accounts. Net worth: total assets minus total liabilities on a particular date.

questions.question: Calculate the net worth: house R500 000, car R80 000, savings R12 000, furniture R30 000; bond R350 000, car loan R50 000, store account R4 000.
questions.expected_answer: Total assets = R622 000. Total liabilities = R404 000. Net worth = R622 000 − R404 000 = R218 000.

questions.question: Give two ways a person can increase their net worth and explain why a high income does not guarantee a high net worth.
questions.expected_answer: Ways (any two): save and invest regularly; pay off debt (highest interest first); avoid unnecessary credit; buy assets that hold value. A high earner who spends everything and has large debts can have low or negative net worth, because net worth depends on what is kept (assets minus liabilities), not what is earned.
